clue.text: Generals about to eat one cabbage

indicators.note: the generals-plus-about pair swallows the next piece, so it is taken inside them

parts.note: top brass, or simply brass, is slang for high-ranking officers
CA (circa) is the Latin abbreviation for about
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Senior officers are about to tuck into a cabbage for dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to eat' puts I inside BRASS + CA, between the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Brassica is the plant genus that includes cabbages, sprouts and broccoli; the cabbage is one member.

clue.text: Full glass of wine may go to the head

explanation.surface: A generous glass of wine can make you tipsy.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a car's bumper, fitted at the front or head of the vehicle, not wine going to your head.
explanation.definitionFit: A brimming glass is a toast-sized bumper; a car's bumper is the bar at its front end.

clue.text: It's hard going from where the butts are — you can get lost!

indicators.note: the letter for hard goes away from the container named next

parts.note: cigarette butts are stubbed out in an ashtray
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A warning that the walk from the shooting butts is tough and confusing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butts' suggests archery targets or grouse shooting; here they are cigarette ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Gone astray means off course and missing.

clue.text: Withdraws with minor injuries

explanation.surface: Pulling out of a race because of some cuts and bruises.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse or competitor scratched is pulled from an event; scratches are also small surface wounds.

clue.text: Where Destiny with Men for Pieces played (Omar Khayyam)

definitions.text: Where Destiny with Men for Pieces played (Omar Khayyam)

parts.words: Where Destiny with Men for Pieces played (Omar Khayyam)
parts.note: a line from FitzGerald's Rubaiyat of Omar Khayyam picturing fate moving people like counters on a game board of nights and days

explanation.surface: A quotation asking where fate played a game using people as its pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: The Rubaiyat line runs: ''Tis all a ... of Nights and Days / Where Destiny with Men for Pieces plays'.
explanation.definitionFit: Draughts and chess are played on a board of alternating squares, the image FitzGerald used for life.

clue.text: Headgirl in tree

parts.note: nut is slang for the head
Meg is a girl's name, short for Margaret

explanation.surface: A head girl sitting up in a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Headgirl' is run together to look like one school title; split it into Head and girl.
explanation.definitionFit: The nutmeg is an evergreen tropical tree whose seed gives the spice.

clue.text: Standard in American university — depressing a student

indicators.note: in a down clue, pressing down means placing the last pieces below the first ones

parts.note: L, for learner, stands for a student

explanation.surface: A normal sight at a US college: a student getting the blues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depressing' is an indicator in a down clue: A and L go underneath US + U.
explanation.definitionFit: Standard and usual both mean normal, as customarily done.

clue.text: Threatening alliance with encirclement by road and rail

indicators.note: the alliance is surrounded by the road and rail pieces

parts.note: the M1 is the main motorway north from London, written MI here
RY is the abbreviation for railway
NATO is the North Atlantic alliance

explanation.surface: A menacing military alliance closing in by road and rail.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is Britain's first and best-known motorway, London to Yorkshire; the digit 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Minatory means menacing, expressing a threat.

clue.text: Did .Claudius get Durer's representation of her?

indicators.note: the letters are represented in a new arrangement

parts.note: the painter's name, its possessive 's adding no letter

explanation.surface: Did Hamlet's uncle get a portrait of his queen from the artist Durer?
explanation.walkthrough: In Hamlet, Claudius marries Gertrude, the prince's mother; 'representation of' rearranges GETDURER.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet's mother, who marries King Claudius, is the woman the clue's pronoun points to.

clue.text: Real-time replacement of army equipment

indicators.note: replacing the letters means putting them back in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Live, up-to-the-minute resupply of an army's kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replacement of' rearranges the eight letters of REALTIME.
explanation.definitionFit: Matériel is the stock of weapons, vehicles and supplies an armed force uses.

clue.text: It ends by .shooting an escapee

explanation.surface: Something finishes by firing a gun at a fleeing prisoner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shooting' is gardening, not gunfire: a runner is a creeping stem that ends by sending up a new plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant runner is a stolon whose tip shoots and roots; a runner is also someone who has run off.

clue.text: Military command to undertake — weapons needed

parts.note: to shoulder a task is to undertake it
arms are weapons

explanation.surface: An order to take on a mission, with guns required.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the drill order to bring a rifle up against the shoulder.

clue.text: Spot-on old-time variety performance

parts.note: ex- means former, of an old time
an act is a turn on a variety bill

explanation.surface: Praise for a faithful revival of a music-hall turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Spot-on and exact both mean precisely correct.

clue.text: Acid. test — no overcoat worn in pad

indicators.note: things worn in a coat are placed inside it, so the coat goes round the other pieces

parts.note: an ulster is a long, loose belted overcoat
pH is the measure that tests how acidic something is
O is nought, a zero, so it stands for no

explanation.surface: A drug trial in a flat, done with the coat off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Acid test' looks like the idiom for a decisive trial, and 'no overcoat' reads as one phrase; split them: PH and O go inside ULSTER.
explanation.definitionFit: To pad furniture with stuffing and fabric is to upholster it.

clue.text: Pure although unrefined loaves, we hear

parts.note: tho' is the informal shortening of although
rough means crude or unrefined

indicators.note: the word for loaves is taken only as it sounds, so its spelling changes

parts.note: loaves are bread

explanation.surface: Wholesome, even if the loaves are coarse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' turns BREAD into the sound-alike BRED.
explanation.definitionFit: A thoroughbred is of pure breeding, with no mixed ancestry.

clue.text: Deal, with objection to moustache

parts.note: to handle a problem is to deal with it
a bar is an obstacle or objection

explanation.surface: Coping with complaints about someone's facial hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A handlebar moustache is a broad one curled up at the ends like a bicycle's bars.

clue.text: Understand garden is to be ploughed up for some food

parts.note: sc., for Latin scilicet, means namely, literally one may understand

indicators.note: ploughing turns the soil over, so the letters of the plot are churned into a new order

explanation.surface: Turning over a garden plot to grow some food.
explanation.walkthrough: SCRAG END is a cheap bony cut of mutton neck, a British butcher's term.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrag end is the neck of mutton, cheap meat for stews.

clue.text: Summary of book in proof form

explanation.surface: A book's synopsis appearing in galley proofs.
explanation.definitionFit: An argument is a synopsis of a book's contents; it is also a chain of reasoning that demonstrates something.

clue.text: Courted lover?

parts.note: not a wooed sweetheart but a lover brought into court, named in a divorce case alongside the unfaithful spouse

explanation.surface: A lover who has been wooed.
explanation.definitionFit: In a divorce for adultery, the person accused of the affair is cited as a party to the case with the spouse.

clue.text: Several horses right to take for a ride outside

indicators.note: the con word goes round the letter for right

parts.note: to sting someone is to swindle them

explanation.surface: A rider choosing among horses to take out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take for a ride' looks like horse riding but means to con.
explanation.definitionFit: A string is the group of racehorses kept by one stable or owner.

clue.text: Why one may have had a dry old Christmas?

definitions.text: Why one may have had a dry old Christmas?

parts.words: Why one may have had a dry old Christmas?
parts.note: split, the answer would explain a dry time: there was no water source; whole, it is an old word for the festive season

explanation.surface: Asking why someone had a boring, booze-free festive season.
explanation.definitionFit: Nowell, or Noel, is an archaic name for Christmas, as in the carol.

clue.text: 18 perhaps grown up but showing signs' of hesitation

parts.note: an adult is someone grown up
er is the sound of hesitating, and two of them are needed

explanation.surface: Someone mature but stammering, um and er.
explanation.walkthrough: 18 is CORESPONDENT, the lover cited in a divorce, who is an example of someone committing adultery.
explanation.definitionFit: A co-respondent is the third party in an adultery case, so is one kind of cheating partner.

clue.text: Chance of a score in Test

definitions.text: Chance of a score in Test

parts.words: Chance of a score in Test
parts.note: read as rugby, a try is a score in a Test match; the phrase is also a chancer's attempt to get away with something

explanation.surface: The chance of scoring in an international rugby match.
explanation.definitionFit: A try-on is a cheeky attempt to see what one can get away with, a punt or gamble.

clue.text: Many people take to this game .

parts.note: a lot is a large number of people

explanation.surface: A remark that this game is popular with lots of folk.
explanation.definitionFit: Lotto is a game of chance like bingo, with numbers drawn at random.

clue.text: War diarist, do we hear?

parts.note: War said aloud is the surname of a novelist who kept diaries; his first name is shared with a seventeenth-century diarist

explanation.surface: Asking whether someone kept a journal during the war.
explanation.walkthrough: Evelyn Waugh (said like 'war') was a novelist and diarist; John Evelyn was the famous 17th-century English diarist.
explanation.definitionFit: John Evelyn kept a celebrated diary of Restoration England, and the novelist Waugh shared the forename.

clue.text: Not straightforward, but giving a sign to the initiated

parts.note: the crab is the zodiac sign Cancer
those in the know are wise to it

explanation.surface: An indirect way of signalling to insiders.
explanation.definitionFit: Crabwise means moving sideways, so indirectly rather than head-on.

clue.text: Taking out as nearly obsolete

explanation.surface: Removing something because it is almost out of use.
explanation.definitionFit: Going out with someone on romantic outings is one sense; becoming old-fashioned is the other.

clue.text: Elaborate altars incorporating silver moulding

indicators.note: the rearranged letters take the next piece into their body
to elaborate is to work something up, so the letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Ornate church altars with silver decorative trim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elaborate' rearranges ALTARS to ASTRAL, and 'incorporating' puts AG inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An astragal is a small rounded architectural moulding, often a bead round a column.
